Recalling exact per-category counts for a specific Unicode version is hard, so this is an estimate built from approximate memory and rough reasoning.

- Nonspacing marks (Mn) are one of the larger combining-mark categories. Their count has grown across Unicode versions as scripts with combining diacritics were added. My recollection puts the Mn total somewhere around 1,950 to 2,000 in the 13.x to 15.x range.
- Unicode 15.1 added 627 characters, but nearly all were ideographs (Lo) in CJK Extension I, plus a few symbols (So). That means the Mn count barely changed from 15.0.
- Unicode 15.0 added scripts such as Tangsa, Toto, Kaktovik numerals, and Vithkuqi, which contributed some Mn characters, so the total stayed close to the figure I half-remember.

My point estimate is about 1,996. For the intervals, my memory is fuzzy by perhaps ±30 to ±50, so I'm giving a 50% interval of roughly 1,975 to 2,010 and a 90% interval of roughly 1,940 to 2,040.
